drafted_from: tool:edit-a-copy-of-a-premiere-project row, do-work/premiere_insert.py and test/test_edit_a_copy.py (test_cut_and_move_write_a_checked_copy_and_record_it) with test/synthetic_prproj.py; the answer was observed by running the command on that made-up project
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a copy of my Premiere project film/made-up.prproj as film/out.prproj with the 2 seconds from 00:00:02:00 cut out and the clip A002 from seconds 10 to 12 moved to the start, and keep the record of what you wrote in film/written.json." It writes the plan, runs the tool and tells you the new length.
no_lists_because: It reads a Premiere project file and a plan file and writes a new project file and a record of outputs; it names no list of yours.
instructions: 1. Choose your project (the .prproj stays untouched), a NEW output name and a written record file in your film folder, and write the plan: {"project": "film/made-up.prproj", "output": "film/out.prproj", "ops": [{"op": "cut", ...}, {"op": "move", ...}]}; ops are insert, cut, move or assemble.
2. Read the tool with tools:list {tool: "tool:edit-a-copy-of-a-premiere-project"}, then from the root of the Workshop checkout run its command with the plan and --written file.

3. Read the last line: {"result": {"output", "blake3", "written", "replaced", "length", "inserts", "log"}} names the new project and its length; {"error": ...} says what to change (a frame rate, mono audio or a drop-frame timecode it will not guess at).
4. Check the copy with do-work/validate.py and do-work/prdump.py, then open the new project in Premiere; the original is untouched.

worked_examples.title: Cut two seconds and move a clip to the start
worked_examples.ask: Cut 00:00:02:00 to 00:00:04:00 out of my project and put the A002 clip from seconds 10 to 12 first.
worked_examples.given: From tools/edit-a-copy-of-a-premiere-project/test/test_edit_a_copy.py and test/synthetic_prproj.py: the AI runs `python3 tools/edit-a-copy-of-a-premiere-project/do-work/premiere_insert.py film/plan.json --written film/written.json` where film/plan.json is {"project": "film/made-up.prproj", "output": "film/out.prproj", "ops": [{"op": "cut", "range": {"from": "00:00:02:00", "to": "00:00:04:00"}}, {"op": "move", "range": {"clip": "A002", "src_in": 10, "src_out": 12}, "to": {"before": {"clip": "A001", "src_in": 0, "src_out": 1}}}]}. The made-up project is 20 s at 23.976 fps with A001.mov (10 s) then A002.mov (10 s from source second 5) on V1 and A1. I ran this exact plan, so the answer is observed.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"output": "film/out.prproj", "blake3": "<64 hex digits of the new file>", "written": "film/written.json", "replaced": null, "length": "00:00:18:00", "inserts": [], "log": ["cut : 00:00:02:00 -> 00:00:04:00", "  2 ranges, 2 items razored, 2 items removed, length 00:00:20:00 -> 00:00:18:00", "move : 00:00:13:00 -> 00:00:15:00 to 00:00:00:00", "  3 ranges, 2 items razored, 0 items removed, length 00:00:18:00 -> 00:00:18:00"]}}. The copy's V1 reads A002.mov 00:00:00:00-00:00:02:00, A001.mov to 00:00:04:00 and 00:00:10:00, A002.mov to 00:00:15:00 and 00:00:18:00 (5 items), A1 matches it, and the input project is byte for byte unchanged.
